paper_metadata.title: Grain refinement of non-equiatomic Cr-rich CoCrFeMnNi high-entropy alloys through combination of cold rolling and precipitation of σ phase

evidence.quote: Grain refinement of non -equiatomic Cr -rich CoCrFeMnNi high -entropy alloys with an fcc structure was studied focusing on the precipitation of a Cr -rich  phase along grain boundaries and shear bands.

the microstructure and mechanical properties of equiatomic and non-equiatomic CoCrFeMnNi HEAs subjected to cold rolling followed by annealing were examined, focusing on the Cr content and the annealing conditions.

mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1273 K for 1 h after 90% cold rolling

evidence.quote: the grain boundary pi nning by the  phase which exhibits a rapid precipitation along the shear bands and the fcc grain boundaries leads to the grain refinement of the fcc matrix in the 25Cr.

mechanisms.name: precipitation strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1273 K for 1 h after 90% cold rolling

evidence.quote: the significant increase in the y of the 25Cr with the  phase is attributed not only to the grain refinement of the fcc matrix but also to the s trengthening caused by the  phase (precipitation strengthening) .

mechanisms.name: grain boundary strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1273 K for 1 h after 90% cold rolling

evidence.quote: The alloys with this fine microstructure containing the  phase exhibit high strength over a wide temperature range due to grain boundary strengthening and precipitation strengthening caused by the  phase.

mechanisms.name: deformation-induced twinning
mechanisms.material_state: tensile-deformed to 10% strain at room temperature

evidence.section: 3.3 Mechanical properties of recrystallized alloys at room temperature
evidence.quote: Deformation-induced twins can be observed in both alloys after the deformation (Fig. 8 (b), (d) ), suggesting that the large ductility of the alloys is closely related to the deformation-induced twinning [28].

mechanisms.name: solid solution strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: recrystallized, annealed at 1273 K for 1 h after 90% cold rolling

evidence.quote: it is supposed that the fast precipitation of precipitates at grain boundaries is one of the features of non-equiatomic HEAs.

mechanisms.name: transformation-induced plasticity (TWIP) effect
mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1273 K for 1 h after 90% cold rolling

evidence.quote: the low SFE of the 25Cr is favorable for the formation of deformation twins, which enhances the ductility of the alloy by the TWIP effect.

mechanisms.name: precipitation strengthening
mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1273 K for 1 h after 90% cold rolling

evidence.quote: The high strength of the 25Cr results from the Hall-Petch effect and precipitation strengthening caused by the sigma phase.

mechanisms.name: Hall-Petch effect
mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1273 K for 1 h after 90% cold rolling

evidence.quote: The high strength of the 25Cr results from the Hall-Petch effect and precipitation strengthening caused by the sigma phase.

mechanisms.name: grain boundary pinning
mechanisms.material_state: annealed at 1273 K for 1 h after 90% cold rolling

evidence.quote: the fast precipitation of the sigma phase results in the suppression of the grain growth of the fcc matrix by the grain boundary pinning, which is consistent with the modified Zener-Smith model.
